title: Legal redlines scratchpad - Inference contract (notes)
content:
Quick scratchpad for negotiating inference contract with Acme. Mostly TODOs and talking points; not polished.

Context / ask:
- Customer wants dedicated inference with access to model variants + optional private deployment.
- They pushed back on our no-training clause (want ability to fine-tune using their data).
- Pricing: committed reserved capacity + overage. SLA with credits.

Top clauses to watch (initial pass):
1) Data usage / training prohibition
   - Our position: no customer data used to train or improve public models. Allow product telemetry/aggregate metrics for product ops only if anonymized.
   - Customer asks to permit fine-tuning on their data (bring-your-own-model or private finetuning).
   - Negotiation point: allow explicit, opt-in fine-tuning under separate SOW with dedicated infra and clear data separation + fee. Insert "no derivative models used for general product training" clause.

2) IP & output ownership
   - Customers expect ownership of outputs. Acceptable to grant them rights to outputs.
   - Carveout: no assignment of model weights or our proprietary model improvements.
   - Ensure license for outputs is "perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free" for customer but preserve our model/IP.

3) Liability / damages cap
   - Standard: cap liability at fees paid in prior 12 months. Oppose open-ended consequential damages.
   - Customer pushing for higher cap or carveouts for IP indemnity.
   - Talk track: mutual indemnity for IP claims; carveouts for customer's data that contains third-party IP.

4) Indemnity scope
   - We should push for narrow indemnity: infringement claims only if claim arises from our model code or infrastructure.
   - Exclude indemnity for outputs that reproduce copyrighted content if customer supplied that content.

5) SLA / service credits vs liquidated damages
   - Keep service credits as sole remedy for SLA failures. Resist liquidated damages language.
   - Define latency targets per route/model, P95 and P99. Do not accept refunds that exceed total fees.

6) Security & audit rights
   - Customer requests broad audit rights. Offer SOC2 report + annual penetration test summary instead of on-site audits.
   - KMS/CMEK support: require prod-level key management for private deployments.
   - CV: 30-day notice for security incidents, 72 hours for breaches that expose customer data.

7) Subprocessors / subcontractors
   - Need standard subprocessors clause with notice and right to object for high-risk subprocessors.
   - Private deployments: if customer requires dedicated hardware, subprocessors list should be limited.

8) Data retention and deletion
   - Define retention for logs, KV cache, and telemetry. Propose delete on termination within 90 days for customer data (shorter for private deployments).
   - Clear obligations for deletion certificates if requested.

9) Export controls / regulated data
   - Add carveouts for regulated data (HIPAA, export-controlled info). If customer wants HIPAA, require BAAs and separate implementation plan.

10) Transition / termination assistance
   - Request: 90 days transition assistance at standard/discounted rates, export of customer data in machine-readable format, no holdback on logs required by us for legal reasons.

11) Pricing & termination for convenience
   - If they want termination for convenience, insist on minimum commitment periods or early termination fees to protect reserved capacity.

12) Confidentiality & publicity
   - Mutual NDA. Customer wants to publicize the partnership; require approval for co-marketing.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How to handle KV cache: is it considered customer data? (Prefer: yes, but ephemeral storage may be excluded for performance reasons; explicit retention windows)
- Model updates: can we update model weights and push new versions without re-consent? Suggest: can push non-breaking updates; material behavior changes require notice / optional opt-out period.
- Metrics & monitoring: define what we share (per-route cost/latency) vs what is internal. Customer asked for token-level breakdown — ok, provide aggregated per-route and per-model not raw token logs.

Negotiation playbook (short):
- Hard lines: no training on customer data unless separate SOW; limit liability to fees paid (12 months); SLA remedies = credits only; no model weight/IP transfer.
- Concede early: provide SOC2 + pen-test, support for CMEK in private deployments, transition assistance.
- Middle ground: allow fine-tuning with strict controls + additional fees and dedicated infra + contractual language preventing general product use.

Draft language snippets to try in redline:
- "Customer Data" means any data provided by Customer to Redwood for the purpose of receiving the Services. Redwood shall not use Customer Data to train, improve or otherwise develop models for Redwood’s general products or services, except as expressly agreed in a separate written statement of work that includes technical and commercial terms.
- "SLA Credits" shall be Customer’s sole and exclusive remedy for any failure to meet the Service Levels.
- "Liability Cap" shall be limited to the aggregate Fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the Order Form during the 12 months preceding the claim.

Notes to self / action items:
- Ask Jason Wu to draft a short clause for CMEK and data partitioning for fine-tuning SOW.
- Connect with infra lead (Avery) to get SLA P95/P99 numbers for dedicated vs hosted so we don't overpromise. Link: CONFLUENCE-ENG-INF-1234.
- Run list of subprocessors and prepare redline with limited objection mechanics.
- Decide fallback for audit: SOC2 + FHIR for healthcare? (if HIPAA required)
- Create playbook table mapping customer asks -> redwood responses for negotiation.

Slack refs: #contracts, #privacy, thread with Acme procurement dated 2025-11-19.

Rough timeline:
- Draft redline to customer by 2025-11-25.
- Expect 2–3 rounds of negotiation, aim to close before end of Q1 2026 if enterprise procurement items (BAA) not required.

Misc messy notes (brain dump):
- Customer asked for "all logs forensics" — push back. Offer time-limited forensics export with NDA + cost recovery.
- They asked for use-case in clause for outputs (e.g., medical summaries). Make sure disclaimers included for non-deterministic outputs.
- Consider adding explicit "no guarantees on factual accuracy" language and a recommended customer responsibility to vet outputs for high-risk domains.

End of scratchpad.

TODO: tidy up into a redlineable doc, add tracked-changes snippets for core clauses (data use / liability / sla).
